note: The record behind tools/rv-water-filter.html. A value fills a main field only when a maker's own document or a maker's own domain states it; anything found only in retailer copy stays in 'retailer_only' and is never printed, and an attribute no maker publishes is named in 'not_published' so the tool can say so rather than leave a blank that reads like an omission. 'gaps' names the makers whose useful numbers are known to exist but whose document URL was not captured, so a later pass knows where to look instead of guessing. Source class 'MAKER' means the maker's own domain; 'MAKER-DOC-3P-HOST' means a document the maker wrote, hosted on a distributor's domain because the maker does not publish it.

winter.rule: Protect the filter from freezing, do not winterize with antifreeze of any type, and store it capped in a refrigerator

Do not allow antifreeze to flow through the filter; take the filter out of the coach and put it in the winterizing bypass hose that came with the system, and store it in a sealed bag with water covering it, not colder than 35 degrees F
Protect the housing against freezing to prevent cracking of the filter and water leakage
Put the filter in a sealed bag with some water left in it and keep it somewhere cool such as a refrigerator, and do not freeze the filter
If the system will not be used for a month or more, unscrew the canisters, empty the water and remove the elements to dry storage in sealed bags

failures.symptom: the filter leaks at the inlet as soon as the water is turned on
failures.cause: 3/4 inch NPT was forced onto a 3/4 inch garden hose thread fitting; the outside diameters are close enough to engage part way and the threads cross
failures.fix: match the thread: garden hose thread seals on a washer, NPT needs an adapter and thread sealant, and the two never screw together

failures.symptom: the new cartridge is the right length and will not seat, or it floats and water bypasses it
failures.cause: 4.5 inch and 2.5 inch cartridges are different formats and neither will seal in the other's housing
failures.fix: measure the cartridge coming out: diameter and length, and check the end cap type

failures.symptom: a 20 inch cartridge bought for a 10 inch housing
failures.cause: the nominal length is the housing size, not a cartridge that will fit any bowl
failures.fix: a 20 inch cartridge never goes in a 10 inch housing

failures.symptom: hot water arrives slowly and the tank takes a long time to fill after the filter was fitted
failures.cause: the low flow class of inline filter is rated at about half a gallon per minute, which is enough for a tap and slow for a tank
failures.fix: choose by flow rate, not only by microns, when the filter has to fill a fresh water tank

rules.rule: Within one diameter family cartridges interchange; across the 2.5 inch to 4.5 inch boundary they do not, and a slim line cartridge will float and bypass in a Big Blue housing
A 20 inch cartridge never goes in a 10 inch housing
Slim line cartridges interchange across housing brands as long as the end cap type matches, double open end or single open end
No maker publishes a cross-brand part-number fitment claim, so this tool never states that a named cartridge fits another maker's named housing
A nominal 10 inch cartridge is about 9.75 to 9.88 inches long, because the housing end caps and the O-ring take the difference; measure the actual cartridge
The arrow on the filter body points in the direction of water flow, and every maker that prints one says to follow it
